summary: Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Geneva around 1992. He held posts at the University of Geneva, Hanazono University (~1992–2004), and the University of Hawaii (~2008).

Michel Strickmann (1942–1994) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Leiden, Paris Diderot, and the EPHE under Hulsewé, Zürcher, Vos, Kaltenmark, Stein, Vandermeersch, and Schipper, later holding posts at UC Berkeley, Bordeaux, and Berlin.
Michela Clemente is a Tibetologist who studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and Hildegard Diemberger. From 2013 to 2015, she served as a Marie Sklodowska Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.
Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He succeeded Giacomo Lignana in 1870 and held a post at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" from circa 1876 to 1914.

Michelle C. Wang is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Eugene Y. Wang (~2002–2008) and became an assistant professor in Art and Art History at Georgetown University around 2012.

Michelle Spuler (1971–) is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Queensland (~1996–2000). She later taught at Victoria University of Wellington and Colorado College.

Michihiko Komine (1945–) studied at Taisho University (~1964–1974) and later worked there (~1974–2016). Specializing in Buddhist studies, he also held posts at the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies and Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Michihiko Yajima (1963–) is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied as a graduate student at the University of Tokyo until 1981. He held posts at the University of Tokyo and Tsurumi University (~2000).

Michihiro Ikeda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held appointments at Komazawa Junior College, Setagaya Gakuen High School, and served as librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies until 2005.

Michiko Yusa (1951–) works in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. She completed her PhD under Raimon Panikkar at UC Santa Barbara (~1977–1983) and served as a professor of Foreign Languages at Western Washington University (~1983–2019).

Michio Kamikawa (1960–) is a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from around 1978 to 1987 and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University from approximately 1993 to 2016.

Michio Yano (1944–) is an Indologist and historian. After studying at Kyoto University and Brown University under David Pingree, he served as a professor in the Faculty of Cultural Studies at Kyoto Sangyo University from around 1975 to 2014.

Michitoshi Barada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Jien Abe and under J. R. Joshi at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1997. Barada has held positions at Otani University and the Eastern Institute.
Michiya Ito was a graduate student at Tohoku University and subsequently held a post there.
Michiyo Hoshi (1941–) is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics who held research appointments at Toyo Bunko and the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa.
Midori Nishino, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University and subsequently held a research post there.

Migmar Tsering (1956–1999) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche (~1974–1985). He served as head of Sakya College (~1989–1998) and held posts at Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and CIHTS.

Mikaël Bauer specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Noritoshi Aramaki, under Paul Hoornaert at Kanazawa University (~2001–2004), and completed his PhD under Ryuichi Abe at Harvard University (~2004–2010).

Mikel Burley studied at Essex under J. M. Bernstein and Bristol under John Peacock, Jonardon Ganeri, and Brian Carr. Working in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, he became Associate Professor of Religion and Philosophy at Leeds in 2005.
Mikio Otsuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who has served as a professor at Hanazono University and as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji.
